title: [Acquired von Willebrand syndrome associated with mechanical circulatory support].
authors: Kenki Saito
journal: [Rinsho ketsueki] The Japanese journal of clinical hematology
abstract: Acquired von Willebrand syndrome (AVWS) is an acquired hemostatic abnormality characterized by quantitative or qualitative defects of von Willebrand factor (VWF). In high-shear conditions, such as aortic stenosis (AS) or mechanical circulatory support (MCS), excessive proteolytic cleavage of von Willebrand factor (VWF) by its specific protease ADAMTS13 leads to the loss of large-molecular-weight VWF multimers. AVWS is increasingly recognized as a potential risk factor for bleeding in patients on MCS. Current management strategies for AVWS associated with MCS include VWF supplementation with fresh frozen plasma or VWF concentrate; however, the therapeutic effect is only transient due to persistent VWF degradation. Our research group developed a humanized anti-ADAMTS13 antibody (HA10), and we are currently developing a novel therapeutic strategy to control bleeding symptoms associated with AVWS by inhibiting ADAMTS13 activity. We demonstrated the efficacy of HA10 in inhibiting VWF degradation in MCS-implanted male cynomolgus monkeys and further established its safety profile in a GLP-grade single-dose intravenous toxicity study in male cynomolgus monkeys. Our data indicate a potentially low risk of thrombotic thrombocytopenic purpura, a potentially severe complication associated with HA10.

title: Rationale for Early Discontinuation of Aspirin After Transcatheter Aortic Valve Implantation: Design of the SOLOTAVI Randomized Trial.
authors: Farzin Beygui; Christophe Caussin; Stéphanie Marlière; Guillaume Bonnet; Eric Durand; Thibaud Lhermusier; Jean-Francois Morelle; Stéphane Delépine; Géraud Souteyrand; Said Ghostine; Eric Van Belle; Olivier Barthélémy; Mariama Akodad; Guillaume Cayla; Chekrallah Chamandi; Frank Chemouni; Jean-Jacques Parienti; Claire Bouleti; Hélène Eltchaninoff; SOLOTAVI Investigators
abstract:
Trans-aortic valve implantation (TAVI) has become the first line treatment of aortic stenosis, a condition predominantly affecting elderly patients. In absence of a specific indication for antithrombotic therapy, lifetime aspirin is recommended after TAVI while it may be discontinued 3 months after bioprosthetic surgical valve replacement. Primary prevention, using aspirin compared to placebo among elderly patients is associated with an increased risk of major bleeding and no reduction rates of thrombotic events. Hence, there is a gap of knowledge on whether aspirin should be continued >3 months after TAVI.
SOLOTAVI is a multicenter, open label, blinded endpoint assessment, 1:1 randomized, non-inferiority trial comparing aspirin discontinuation 3 months after TAVI (experimental) to long-term therapy (control). Adult patients with successful transfemoral TAVI for symptomatic aortic stenosis and no indication or contraindication for long-term antithrombotic therapy will be enrolled. Randomization is stratified on center and valve type. The primary endpoint is the 12-month composite of all cause death, myocardial infarction, stroke, and non-procedure-related major or disabling bleeding. A hierarchical analysis is performed for the primary and 3 principal secondary endpoints. The sample size is computed for demonstrating the non-inferiority of the experimental strategy compared with the control strategy, with a conservative non-inferiority margin of 6.5%. A total of 1400 patients will be enrolled.
The SOLOTAVI trial will assess the non-inferiority of a 3-month duration of aspirin compared to the long-term therapy after successful transfemoral TAVI in terms of thrombotic and bleeding events. NCT06518317 clinicaltrials.org.

title: Carotid Endarterectomy Versus Trans-Carotid Artery Revascularisation (TCAR) for Asymptomatic Carotid Stenosis A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis.
authors: Karina Domingos Rosa Schneidwind; Reza Mofidi
abstract:
The treatment for asymptomatic carotid artery stenosis includes a surgical or interventional approach in selected cases. Although endarterectomy should be considered over stenting for selected patients, according to the latest European Society of Vascular Surgery (ESVS) guidelines, the Carotid Revascularization and Medical Management for Asymptomatic Carotid Stenosis Trials (CREST-2) suggested that carotid stenting would be associated with low rates of perioperative stroke or death. The transcarotid artery revascularization (TCAR) technique is a relatively new endovascular method, which involves placing a stent at the carotid bifurcation through direct carotid artery access, performed under a flow reversal system. This approach avoids manipulation of the aortic arch, potentially reducing embolic events. The aim of this systematic review is to compare TCAR with carotid endarterectomy (CEA) in asymptomatic patients undergoing carotid intervention. It seeks to evaluate whether TCAR is associated with improved perioperative outcomes, such as lower rates of stroke and death, compared with CEA, given its potentially less invasive approach.
The review was performed according to the Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses (PRISMA) on the platforms PubMed/Medline, OVID/Embase, and Scopus. The following MeSH terms were used: "asymptomatic carotid stenosis" AND "carotid endarterectomy", "transcarotid artery revascularization" OR "TCAR". Full-text screening and data extraction were performed with the support of the COVIDENCE platform. Six studies were selected for this systematic review, comprising a total of 132,684 patients (30,581 undergoing TCAR and 102,103 undergoing CEA). Statistical analysis was performed using R software.
The selected studies for this systematic review showed similar results in terms of perioperative stroke and death for asymptomatic patients who underwent carotid endarterectomy and TCAR.
Our results suggest that there are no significant differences between CEA and TCAR for the treatment of asymptomatic patients who require a surgical or interventional approach. Further studies are necessary to provide more robust data in this field.

title: Echocardiographic atrial and right heart to pulmonary circulation coupling indices identify high-risk in moderate aortic stenosis.
authors: Gloria Santangelo; Andrea Faggiano; Giulio Pio Federico Mallardi; Michele Baroni; Luca Donisi; Alessandro Guareschi; Guido Pasero; Fabiola Sozzi; Massimiliano Ruscica; Marco Guazzi; Stefano Carugo; Francesca Bursi
abstract:
Emerging evidence points on an increased mortality risk associated to moderate aortic stenosis (AS), yet this population remains insufficiently characterized. We tested the prognostic value of two echocardiographic coupling indices reflecting right and left-sided cardiac function: the ratio of tricuspid annular plane systolic excursion to pulmonary artery systolic pressure ratio (TAPSE/PASP) and the left atrial volumetric/mechanical coupling index (LACI).
Retrospective, single-center study including 135 patients with moderate AS. TAPSE/PASP was used as a non-invasive surrogate of right ventricular-pulmonary circulation (RV-Pc) coupling, and LACI was defined as ratio of left atrial volume index to mitral a' velocity. The primary endpoint was all-cause mortality. Cox regression and Kaplan-Meier analyses were used to assess the prognostic value of both indices.
During a mean follow-up of 1.61 ± 0.79 years, 33 patients (24%) died. Reduced TAPSE/PASP (< 0.67 mm/mmHg) and elevated LACI (> 5.17) were independently associated with an increased mortality (HR: 3.03 and 3.16, respectively, p < 0.01). These associations remained significant even after adjusting for age. Stratification into three groups - preserved, single, or combined uncoupling -showed progressively lower 1-year survival rates, ranging from 95% to 49% (p < 0.0001). None of the coupling-derived variables was associated with hemodynamic progression or need of aortic valve replacement.
TAPSE/PASP and LACI are independently associated with mortality in patients with moderate AS. These parameters may provide incremental prognostic information in this often-overlooked population. These findings may prompt further studies evaluating the potential role of these parameters in helping to refine prognostic phenotyping.

title: The Hidden Danger of Aortic Stenosis-Exercise-Induced Cardiac Arrest in a Young Man with Bicuspid Aortic Valve.
authors: Lars Ege Rasmussen; Christian Alcaraz Frederiksen; Thomas Krusenstjerna-Hafstrøm; Henrik Vase
abstract: • BAoV is the most common congenital heart disease. • Underestimating AS using TTE is rare. • The consequences of underestimating severe AS can be fatal. • Extensive diagnostic workup is advised when symptoms and TTE findings are discordant.

title: Tricuspid aortic valve morphology predicts favorable midterm outcomes after aortic valve neocuspidization in children.
authors: Guanxi Wang; Sen Zhang; Kai Ma; Kunjing Pang; Benqing Zhang; Keming Yang; Shoujun Li
abstract:
To evaluate the midterm outcomes of the aortic valve neocuspidalization (AVNeo) procedure for aortic valve reconstruction in 83 pediatric patients with complex aortic valve disease and to identify risk factors associated with the outcomes.
A retrospective analysis was conducted on pediatric patients who underwent the AVNeo procedure between January 2017 and June 2025. The composite primary end point included all-cause mortality, reoperation, or moderate-to-severe aortic valve dysfunction (regurgitation or stenosis). Univariate and multivariate Cox proportional hazards models were used to identify risk factors.
Among the 83 patients (mean age 7.0 ± 3.7 years; 67.5% male) included in the analysis, the predominant preoperative pathology was moderate-to-severe aortic regurgitation (88.0%). Single-leaflet reconstruction (65.1%) using autologous pericardium (94.0%) was the most common surgical approach. Over a mean follow-up of 28.4 ± 23.9 months, 27 patients (32.5%) met the composite end point, including 2 late deaths, 18 cases of moderate-to-severe regurgitation, and 9 cases of moderate-to-severe stenosis; 10 patients underwent reoperation. The probability of freedom from the primary end point was 83.6%, 64.5%, and 54.4% at 1, 3, and 6 years, respectively. Multivariable analysis identified tricuspid aortic valve morphology as an independent protective factor against the primary end point (hazard ratio, 0.408; 95% CI, 0.178-0.935, P = .034), whereas the use of autologous pericardium showed a strong protective trend (hazard ratio, 0.284; 95% CI, 0.078-1.037, P = .057).
AVNeo provides midterm outcomes that support its use as an alternative strategy. Tricuspid aortic valve morphology is a strong predictor of favorable outcomes, and the use of autologous pericardium demonstrates significant potential as a protective factor.

title: Long-term outcomes of transcatheter versus surgical aortic valve replacement in patients aged 70 years and older: An overlap-weighted analysis.
authors: Rieko Kutsuzawa; Naonori Kawamoto; Kimito Minami; Satoshi Kainuma; Kizuku Yamashita; Kota Suzuki; Takashi Kakuta; Ayumi Ikuta; Yuki Tadokoro; Yojiro Machii; Kentaro Mitsui; Shinichi Kurashima; Yuki Irie; Atsushi Okada; Kensuke Takagi; Makoto Amaki; Hideaki Kanzaki; Yasuhide Asaumi; Takeshi Kitai; Chisato Izumi; Satsuki Fukushima
abstract:
To compare long-term outcomes of transcatheter aortic valve replacement (TAVR) and surgical aortic valve replacement (SAVR) in patients aged 70 to 89 years with aortic stenosis (AS).
In this single-center retrospective study, 1100 patients who underwent primary TAVR (n = 599) or SAVR (n = 501) between 2008 and 2023 were included. An overlap-weighted propensity-score analysis was conducted using 36 baseline variables, including age, procedural year, frailty scale, Society of Thoracic Surgeons risk score, New York Heart Association class, history of coronary artery and cerebrovascular disease, and AS severity. The primary end point was the composite of all-cause mortality or cerebrovascular events.
During long-term follow-up, the composite end point occurred more frequently after TAVR than after SAVR. In the overlap-weighted analysis, TAVR was associated with a greater risk of the composite outcome (hazard ratio [HR], 1.8; 95% CI, 1.1-3.0; P = .024), with Kaplan-Meier curves diverging early and remaining separated. All-cause mortality did not differ between the groups (HR, 1.2; 95% CI, 0.7-2.1; P = .426); however, cerebrovascular events occurred predominantly after TAVR and remained significantly more frequent after overlap weighting (HR, 15; 95% CI, 2.8-89; P = .002).
In the overlap-weighted population of patients aged 70 to 89 years with AS, SAVR and TAVR were associated with comparable all-cause mortality; however, cerebrovascular events occurred more frequently after TAVR.

title: Marked Underreferral to Structural Heart Specialists in Severe Tricuspid Regurgitation Despite High Clinical Burden: An Adjusted Registry Analysis.
authors: Prince Darko; John Costner; Brennan Carter; Baffour Otchere; Christopher Chinnatambi; Papa Beeko; Patrick Berchie; Oladipo Odeyinka; Eunice Hama; Swethapriya Chaparala
journal: Structural heart : the journal of the Heart Team
abstract:
Severe tricuspid regurgitation (TR) carries mortality risk comparable to untreated severe aortic stenosis, yet specialist referral rates remain poorly characterized.
We analyzed 1000 patients with severe TR from CardioCare registry from a single center in Georgia. The primary outcome was the absence of structural heart disease (SHD) specialist evaluation. Multivariable logistic regression identified predictors of referral failure adjusted for age, heart failure (HF), kidney and liver disease, symptoms, right ventricular systolic pressure (RVSP), and ejection fraction, with an extended model adding coronary artery disease, conduction delay, and New York Heart Association (NYHA) class III-IV. Kaplan-Meier and Cox analyses assessed survival by evaluation status and clinical subgroup.
Only 328 patients (32.8%) underwent SHD evaluation despite symptoms (86.4%), HF (86.5%), kidney disease (65.1%), and liver disease (32.0%). HF was the strongest referral predictor (adjusted odds ratio [OR] 0.20, 95% CI 0.11-0.36); NYHA class III-IV, coronary artery disease, and conduction delay were also independently associated, whereas kidney disease, liver disease, and symptoms were not, and higher RVSP paradoxically predicted lower referral (OR 1.02/mmHg; both p < 0.001). Only 13.2% of symptomatic patients without HF were evaluated, and those with combined HF, kidney, and liver disease had the highest mortality (22.4%) but no preferential referral. Survival was worse with HF, increasing organ burden, and RVSP ≥40 mmHg; these factors plus age remained independent mortality predictors on Cox analysis, though this association attenuated in sensitivity analysis.
More than two-thirds of patients with severe TR never reach an SHD specialist despite substantial clinical burden, highlighting the need for echocardiography-triggered referral pathways and quality metrics.

title: Postoperative root size predicts regurgitation in supravalvular aortic stenosis repair.
authors: Dominic P Recco; Lauren Marshall; Matthew Schildmeier; Kimberlee Gauvreau; Joseph Confessore; Luis G Quinonez; Pedro J Del Nido; Christopher W Baird; Peter E Hammer; David M Hoganson
abstract:
Supravalvular aortic stenosis (SVAS) repair carries a moderate risk for postoperative aortic regurgitation (AR). This may be related to the targeted sinotubular junction diameter z score (STJDZ) at reconstruction, traditionally sized to zero. We investigated relationships between achieved STJDZ and aortic valve function after repair.
Sixty-six children underwent patch repair from 2010 to 2024 at a median age of 1.2 years (interquartile range [IQR], 0.4, 3.5 years) via Brom (n = 53), Doty (n = 9), and McGoon (n = 4) techniques. Relationships between STJDZ and aortic valve function were assessed via Jonckheere-Terpstra nonparametric test for trend over median follow-up of 5.6 years (IQR, 2.4, 8.4 years).
Preoperatively, AR was none/trivial in 52 (79%), left ventricular outflow tract obstruction (LVOTO) moderate or greater in 54 (82%), and median STJDZ -3.8 (IQR, -4.4, -2.9). At discharge, AR and LVOTO were mild or greater in 45 (68%) and 18 (27%), and median STJDZ was -0.3 (IQR, -1.3, -1.1). STJDZ increased by a median of 3.0 (IQR, 1.6, 4.4) preoperatively to postoperatively. Discharge AR was none/trivial at median STJDZ -1.3 (IQR, -1.8, -0.1) and worsened with increasing diameters (mild: 0.4 [IQR, -1.0, 1.8], mild+: 0.0 [IQR, -1.2, 1.5]; P = .038), with similar results at follow-up (P = .048). LVOTO worsened with lower median STJDZ (none/trivial: 0.2 [IQR, -1.2, 1.5], mild: -1.3 [IQR, -3.2, -0.1]; P = .015). Subanalysis of those with none/trivial preoperative AR (n = 52) showed that increase in STJDZ by ≥4 demonstrated worse follow-up AR (P = .016).
Achieving STJDZ zero using patch repair techniques to relieve SVAS obstruction demonstrated mild or greater postoperative AR compared with none/trivial regurgitation at median z score -1.3. Mild LVOTO was noted with median z score -1.3. Targeting STJDZ of -1 in pediatric SVAS repair appears appropriate to balance residual regurgitation and LVOTO. Further follow-up is required to understand the long-term impact of this target on aortic growth.

title: Bibliometric and visualized analysis of research trends and knowledge structure in novel pharmacological treatments for hypertrophic cardiomyopathy.
authors: Zhen Chen; Fen Ai; Jinlei Li; Bingxin Cheng; Weihao Cheng; Yu Li
abstract:
This study presents a bibliometric and visual analysis of the literature on novel drug therapies for hypertrophic cardiomyopathy (HCM) to explore recent research trends, hotspots, and developmental directions.
Publications related to novel drug treatments for HCM from 2015 to 2025 were retrieved from the Web of Science Core Collection. CiteSpace and VOSviewer (with standard parameters: time slicing 2015-2025, node selection based on co-occurrence, and pathfinder pruning) were utilized for quantitative and visual analyses.
After screening, 281 publications were included. The annual publication output exhibited an overall upward trend. The United States led in the number of publications, while England played a prominent hub role in international collaboration. The Harvard University system formed a high-yield cluster, and the University of California system served as a key bridge. Co-citation analysis of journals revealed an interdisciplinary knowledge structure spanning basic science to clinical medicine. Both reference and keyword analyses confirmed that the research frontier has shifted from early exploration of the cardiac myosin mechanism to a current focus on myosin inhibitors.
Bibliometric evidence indicates a clear shift toward targeted therapy centered on cardiac myosin inhibitors, marking a transition in research focus. These findings provide a quantitative roadmap for researchers and clinicians to identify key players, collaborative opportunities, and emerging topics. Future studies are expected to deepen focus on non-obstructive HCM, personalized treatment, and long-term efficacy verification.

title: Inter-American consensus on hypertrophic cardiomyopathy.
authors: Josefina B Parodi; Cristhian E Scatularo; Enrique A Berríos-Bárcenas; Juan D López-Ponce de León; Diego Pérez de Arenaza; Luis E Gómez; Juan P Costabel; Fabio Fernandes; Clara Saldarriaga; Víctor Rossel; Carlos E Rochitte; Ricardo Stein; Roberto Concepción-Chacón; Gabriel Parma-Romanelli; Karina González-Carta; Susana Blanco-Sobrino; Daniel Sierra-Lara-Martínez; Franco Leoni; Jorge Jalil; Yamiris Delgado; Diego X Chango; Liliana Posada-Martínez; Landy Rodríguez-Amaguay; Carlos Guamán-Valdivieso; Jairo A Rendón-Giraldo; Víctor Arévalos; Ingrid Márquez; Florencia B Cantora; Mariano D Estofán; Ivonne Cárdenas-Reyes; Noël Brögger; María C Bejarano; Joffre Lara-Terán; Ignacio Vaca-Valverde; Carlos Olivares-Asencio; Leandro Cura-Hochbaum; Paola A Morejón-Barragán; Agostina M Fava; Andrés F Miranda-Arboleda; Manlio F Márquez-Murillo; Eric Karabut; Ana C Berni-Betancourt; Ana C Alba; María J Rodríguez-González; María M Sáenz-Tejeira; Katihurca Almonte-Montes de Oca; Rosa N Cueto; Melissa Rodríguez-Israel; Alicia G Torterolo-Herrera; Vicente Villacreses; Gustavo Restrepo; María I Sosa-Liprandi; Eugenio Cingolani; Sergio Baratta; Ricardo López-Santi; Ana Múnera-Echeverri; Adrián Baranchuk
abstract:
Hypertrophic cardiomyopathy (HCM) is the most common inherited cardiomyopathy and poses major diagnostic and therapeutic challenges in Latin America, owing to heterogeneity in resource availability, access to advanced technologies, and the organization of health systems.
To develop the first Inter-American Consensus on HCM, in order to standardize the care of these patients tailored to the regional context.
The Inter-American Society of Cardiology (SIAC) convened a committee of experts from different countries across the Americas. A systematic review of the evidence was performed, followed by the development of recommendations, which were validated using a formal Delphi methodology; consensus was defined as agreement among more than 80% of participants.
The consensus provides a comprehensive approach to the evaluation and management of HCM. It covers epidemiology, pathophysiology, multimodality diagnostic tools, genetics and family counseling, phenocopies, pharmacological and invasive treatment, associated complications, sudden cardiac death risk assessment, special populations (pediatric and pregnant patients), physical exercise, and follow-up strategies. In addition, it includes specific recommendations aimed at facilitating the implementation of these across Latin America.
The Inter-American Consensus on HCM provides recommendations for the diagnosis and treatment of this condition. It integrates the best available evidence with regional clinical experience and takes into account the epidemiological, economic, and healthcare characteristics of the region. It constitutes a reference framework for standardizing the care of patients with HCM and their families throughout Latin America.

title: Transcriptomics Identifies a Small Set of Circulating Biomarkers and Signaling Pathways Dysregulated in Hypertrophic Cardiomyopathy.
authors: Yuko Kiyohara; Keitaro Akita; Michael A Fifer; Albree Tower-Rader; Sergio Teruya; Bilal Ansari; Alfonsina M Santos; Mathew S Maurer; Yuichi J Shimada
abstract:
It is sometimes challenging to distinguish hypertrophic cardiomyopathy (HCM) from other cardiomyopathies with left ventricular hypertrophy (LVH). At present, no circulating biomarkers to distinguish HCM have been established.
The authors aimed to identify plasma microRNA (miRNA) biomarkers unique to HCM.
In this multicenter case-control study, the authors performed comprehensive plasma transcriptomics profiling in cases with HCM and controls with hypertensive LVH, transthyretin amyloid cardiomyopathy (ATTR-CM), and aortic stenosis (AS). For each disease group, they chronologically split the patients into training and test sets. The authors identified miRNAs that were significantly (Benjamini-Hochberg-adjusted P < 0.05) upregulated or downregulated in HCM compared with hypertensive LVH. They made the same comparisons between HCM and ATTR-CM and between HCM and AS. They determined miRNAs that were consistently upregulated or downregulated in HCM throughout all 3 comparisons. Then, they selected miRNAs independently associated with HCM after adjusting for potential confounders. Using the selected miRNAs, the authors developed a logistic regression model to distinguish HCM in the training set. They calculated the area under the receiver-operating characteristic curve in the test set.
The authors analyzed 2,656 miRNAs in patients with HCM (n = 294), hypertensive LVH (n = 321), ATTR-CM (n = 167), and AS (n = 38). They identified 3 miRNAs (miR-454-3p, miR-98-5p, and miR-5581-3p). The logistic regression model using the 3 miRNAs had an area under the receiver-operating characteristic curve of 0.95 (95% CI: 0.93-0.97) with a sensitivity of 0.95 and a specificity of 0.90 in the test set.
Comprehensive plasma transcriptomics profiling identified a small set of circulating miRNAs to distinguish HCM from other cardiomyopathies with LVH.

title: Predictors of Early Mortality After Open Aorto-Iliac Reconstruction in Patients with Aortoiliac Occlusive Disease: An Observational Cohort Study.
authors: Merei Imanbayev; Altay Dyussupov; Bekzhigit Tussupkanov; Ergali Muratzhanov; Ardak Mautbekova; Dinara Kozubayeva; Rustam Mukhametkhanov; Rail Gafurov; Nurbek Irgebayev; Dainius Pavalkis; Evgeniy Zhuravlev; Yersyn Sabitov
abstract: Background and Objectives: Open aorto-iliac reconstruction (AIR) for aorto-iliac occlusive disease (AIOD) remains a high-risk procedure due to multifocal atherosclerosis affecting coronary, cerebrovascular, and renal arterial beds. This study aimed to identify factors independently associated with 30-day mortality and explore factors associated with late mortality during available follow-up among 30-day survivors following open AIR. Materials and Methods: An observational, non-randomised cohort of 170 consecutive patients undergoing open AIR for AIOD between January 2018 and December 2024 was analysed. Univariate logistic regression was performed for 30-day mortality; given the limited number of events (n = 16), the primary multivariable analysis used penalized likelihood logistic regression (Firth correction). Late survival among 30-day survivors (landmark cohort, n = 154) was analysed using Kaplan-Meier methods and exploratory univariate Cox proportional hazards regression, with surviving patients censored at the last available follow-up; multivariable Cox modelling was not performed due to the limited number of late events (n = 10). Results: Thirty-day mortality was 9.4% (16/170) in the overall cohort. In the primary Firth penalized multivariable logistic regression, factors associated with 30-day mortality were: severe left IIA stenosis ≥ 70% (OR 9.68; 95% CI 3.08-30.43; p = 0.0001), chronic kidney disease (OR 3.62; 95% CI 1.03-12.66; p = 0.044), and increasing aortic cross-clamp duration, analysed continuously (OR 1.022 per minute; 95% CI 1.000-1.045); a conventional ≥60 min categorical threshold showed a consistent secondary association (OR 4.15; 95% CI 1.28-13.46; p = 0.018). Non-inclusion of IIA was associated with increased 30-day mortality on univariate analysis (OR 4.80; 95% CI 1.31-17.62; p = 0.018). Among the 154 patients entering the 30-day landmark cohort, 10 late deaths were observed during available follow-up. In exploratory univariate Cox regression, intraoperative blood loss was the only statistically significant factor associated with late mortality (HR 1.07 per 100 mL; 95% CI 1.03-1.12; p = 0.0006). Conclusions: Severe IIA disease, chronic kidney disease, and increasing aortic cross-clamp duration (analysed continuously) were independently associated with increased 30-day mortality after open AIR. Intraoperative blood loss was associated with late mortality in exploratory univariate survival analysis. These findings require validation in larger prospective cohorts with longer and more uniform follow-up.

title: Unravelling the Diagnosis of Normal-Flow Low-Gradient Aortic Stenosis: The Role of Multimodality Imaging.
authors: Laura Rotondo; Elena Marchetti; Rita Pavasini; Elisabetta Tonet; Carlo Tumscitz; Carlo Penzo; Marta Cocco; Maria Lo Monaco; Erika Bertella; Gianluca Campo; Federico Marchini
abstract: Normal-flow, low-gradient aortic stenosis is one of the most deceptive presentations of aortic stenosis. It leaves clinicians uncertain whether they are facing true severe disease or a measurement artefact. This often reflects a discordant grading pattern, in which many patients ultimately prove to have moderate disease. This diagnostic paradox arises from a combination of measurement errors, geometric assumptions, and genuine hemodynamic complexity, and cannot be resolved by echocardiography alone. A structured multimodality imaging strategy integrating calcium score evaluation on cardiac computed tomography, tissue characterisation on cardiac magnetic resonance and, when necessary, invasive hemodynamic assessment is the only reliable path to diagnostic certainty and appropriate therapeutic decision-making. Together, these modalities form a coherent sequential algorithm that moves from the non-invasive to the invasive, from the hemodynamic to the biological, and from uncertainty to actionable clinical decision. This review provides an updated, critical appraisal of each imaging tool and its respective strengths and pitfalls.

title: Documented Valvular Regurgitation and Explicit Heart Failure in an Internal Medicine Registry: A Cross-Sectional Study.
authors: Maria Rada; Maria-Laura Craciun; Ana-Maria Pah; Diana Utu; Dana Emilia Velimirovici; Diana-Maria Mateescu; Ioana Cotet; Ariana Bianca Velciov; Cristiana Adina Avram
abstract: Background and Objectives: Routine records may conflate valvular heart disease (VHD), functional classification, and shared diagnostic assessment. We quantified the cross-sectional association between a registry VHD label and explicitly documented heart failure (HF), while recognizing that every observed valve lesion was regurgitant. Materials and Methods: The analytic sample comprised all 224 eligible adults admitted to the Internal Medicine II Department of a railway-affiliated hospital between 1 August 2025 and 31 July 2026: 38 with documented VHD and 186 without documented VHD. The primary outcome was an explicit HF diagnosis; a combined HF/NYHA-positive field was examined as an over-inclusive sensitivity outcome. Logistic regression was adjusted for age, sex, body mass index, smoking history, and total cholesterol. Results: Explicit HF was documented in 24/38 patients with VHD (63.2%) and 72/186 without VHD (38.7%; adjusted OR 2.87, 95% CI 1.38-5.99). The combined outcome was present in 28/38 (73.7%) and 101/186 (54.3%), respectively (adjusted OR 2.38, 95% CI 1.09-5.21). All 38 exposed patients had documented mitral, aortic, and/or tricuspid regurgitation; no stenosis, prolapse, or prior valve intervention was recorded. Conclusions: Documented valvular regurgitation was associated with explicit HF documentation. Because regurgitation may be secondary to ventricular or atrial disease, reverse causation, shared ascertainment, non-adjudicated diagnoses, and residual confounding preclude causal, temporal, prognostic, or lesion-specific inference.

title: Sutureless Aortic Valve Replacement with the Perceval Plus® Versus TAVI: A Propensity-Matched Analysis of Postoperative Outcomes, Hematological Dynamics, and Inflammatory Response.
authors: Umit Kahraman; Irem Demiray; Serkan Ertugay; Emrah Oguz; Oguz Yavuzgil; Hakan Posacioglu; Anıl Ziya Apaydin; Ismet Tanzer Calkavur; Mustafa Ozbaran; Tahir Yagdi
abstract: Perceval Plus and TAVI are increasingly used for severe aortic stenosis, both relying on a self-expanding nitinol stent design, yet evidence specific to Perceval Plus remains limited regarding postoperative clinical outcomes and hematological and inflammatory dynamics. We compared postoperative clinical outcomes and longitudinal platelet/CRP dynamics between Perceval Plus and TAVI in a retrospective single-center cohort, in which 26 propensity score-matched pairs were obtained (1:1 matching) from patients undergoing Su-AVR (Perceval Plus, n = 53) or TAVI (self-expanding Medtronic devices, n = 101). Mortality, echocardiographic outcomes, and rates of postoperative atrial fibrillation and conduction disturbances showed no statistically significant differences between groups, while TAVI was associated with shorter ICU and hospital stay and Su-AVR required higher FFP transfusion (p = 0.016). Platelet count declined in both groups, with a deeper nadir in Su-AVR (postoperative day 3: 66% decline) versus TAVI (day 4: 27% decline), with a significant group × time interaction (p = 0.013); CRP rose in both groups but more rapidly and to a greater magnitude in Su-AVR (time and group × time interaction, both p < 0.001). Su-AVR and TAVI showed no statistically significant differences in the clinical safety outcomes assessed but differed in postoperative hematological and inflammatory magnitude, likely reflecting multifactorial procedure- and device-related mechanisms, warranting confirmation in larger, prospective, multicenter studies.

title: Preoperative Ballon Aortic Valvuloplasty vs. Conservative Management in Patients Undergoing Hip Fracture Surgery with Underlying Severe Aortic Stenosis.
authors: Antonio De Vita; Marcello Covino; Francesco Mollo; Matteo Vumbaca; Chiara Napolitano; Saverio Tremamunno; Nello Cambise; Rosaria Natali; Marco Rossi; Tiziana Bove; Raffaele Vitiello; Giulio Maccauro; Francesco Franceschi; Carlo Trani; Francesco Burzotta; Gaetano Antonio Lanza
abstract: Background: Old adults with hip fracture (HFx) and concomitant severe aortic stenosis (AS) represent a high-risk population in whom urgent orthopedic repair is usually required, while definitive valve replacement is rarely feasible preoperatively. The clinical benefit of balloon aortic valvuloplasty (BAV) as a bridging strategy remains uncertain. Methods: In this observational study, we included patients admitted to our Emergency Department for HFx who had concomitant severe AS. Management of severe AS consisted of either conservative therapy or preoperative BAV. The early clinical endpoints included 30-day mortality, time to surgery, length of intensive care unit and hospital stay and need for mechanical ventilation. The late clinical endpoint was 180-day all-cause mortality. Results: Among 3958 patients admitted for HFx fracture, 46 (1.2%) were found to have severe AS and fulfilled the inclusion criteria. Of these, 12 patients (26.1%) underwent preoperative BAV and 34 (73.9%) received conservative management. Thirty-day mortality was 8.3% in the BAV group and 23.5% in the conservative group (HR 0.32; 95%CI 0.04-2.60; p = 0.29). Time to surgery was longer in the BAV group (p < 0.001) with concomitantly longer hospital (p = 0.001) and ICU (p = 0.041) stays. Preoperative BAV was independently associated with lower 180-day mortality (HR 0.13; 95%CI 0.03-0.63; p = 0.011). Conclusions: In patients with severe AS undergoing urgent HFx repair, preoperative BAV was associated with reduced 180-day mortality, suggesting a potential long-term prognostic benefit, which warrants confirmation in larger prospective studies. However, it was not associated with significantly better 30-day survival and was accompanied by surgical delay and greater healthcare resource utilization.

title: Early and Long-Term Results of 101 Consecutive Patients After Transcarotid Transcatheter Aortic Valve Implantation.
authors: Damian Hudziak; Monika Gruz-Kwapisz; Radosław Parma; Wojciech Wańha; Sylwia Gładysz-Wańha; Wojciech Wojakowski; Radosław Gocoł
abstract: Background/Objectives: Transcatheter aortic valve implantation through the common carotid artery (TC-TAVI) is one of the possible treatment options for patients with ineligible transfemoral approach. The aim of our study was to evaluate the efficacy and safety of patients treated with TC-TAVI in early and long-term follow-up. Methods: The study included patients with severe aortic stenosis treated with TC-TAVI. In-hospital outcomes, early, long-term follow-up were presented in accordance with the VARC-3 recommendations. Results: The analysis presented 101 patients. We observed high procedural success-97% (n = 98). The number of VARC-3 incidents: 3.96% major vascular complications; 0.99% myocardial infarction; 0.99% cardiac tamponade; 0.99% life-threatening bleeding; 3.96% cerebrovascular incidents. The NYHA class decreased significantly compared to the pre-procedure value (2 [1-2] vs. 3 [3-3]; p < 0.001). There was a significant improvement in postprocedural cerebral oximetry values compared to baseline on both the implanted and contralateral sides (67.5 [63-71]% vs. 70 [63.5-75]%; p < 0.05) and (67 [64-71]% vs. 71 [64-76]%; p < 0.05), respectively. The 30-day, 1-year, and 2-year survival rates were 94.1%, 80.2%, and 69.3%, respectively. In the univariate analysis, BAV (HR 4.54; 95% CI: 1.14-17.99; p = 0.03) and LVEF ≤ 35% (HR 7.32; 95% CI: 2.59-20.65; p < 0.001) were significantly associated with two-year mortality. In an exploratory adjusted Cox regression analysis, BAV (HR 2.63; 95% CI: 1.07-6.45; p = 0.03) and LVEF ≤ 35% (HR 3.48; 95% CI: 1.67-7.24; p < 0.001) were associated with higher 2-year mortality. Conclusions: Our single-center, observational report indicated feasibility and good observed outcomes of the TC-TAVI procedure in an experienced clinical team.

title: Research trends and hotspot analysis of sudden cardiac death in hypertrophic cardiomyopathy: A bibliometric analysis.
authors: Zhen Chen; Fen Ai; Jinlei Li; Yu Li
abstract:
Hypertrophic cardiomyopathy is the most common genetic heart disease and a leading cause of sudden cardiac death. This study aims to map the research landscape of Hypertrophic cardiomyopathy -related sudden cardiac death over the past 2 decades using bibliometric methods.
We performed a bibliometric analysis of 712 publications retrieved from the Web of Science Core Collection (2005-2025). Using Cite Space, we examined publication trends, collaboration networks, co-citation patterns, and keyword dynamics.
Annual publication output rose markedly, with pronounced accelerations after the 2014 European Society of Cardiology and 2020 American heart association/American College of Cardiology guidelines. The United States led in productivity (203 publications) and network centrality (0.40), while China ranked second in output (123 publications) but exhibited limited international collaboration (centrality = 0.01). Co‑citation analysis indicated that clinical guidelines and risk‑prediction models form the field' score knowledge base, and five of the ten most cited references were international guidelines. Keyword analysis defined 4 principal thematic clusters disease entity, clinical outcomes, imaging biomarkers, and risk stratification and documented a shift from early mechanistic studies to multimodal risk prediction, followed more recently by artificial intelligence-driven models and targeted pharmacological therapies (e.g., mavacamten).
This study provides a systematic, data-driven overview of the knowledge structure and evolutionary trends in Hypertrophic cardiomyopathy-related sudden Cardiac death research. The findings underscore the field' s guideline-driven character, document the rise of AI-based risk stratification, and describe a paradigm shift toward disease-modifying therapies, offering actionable insights for prioritizing future research and informing clinical decision-making.

title: Practical Solutions to Common TAVI Complications
authors: Herbert Kroon
abstract: Aortic valve stenosis Calcific aortic valve degeneration mainly affects the elderly population. Approximately 15% of elderly patients have some degree of aortic stenosis (AS)1. Untreated severe AS will lead to heart failure, angina and/or syncope and approximately half of patients will expire within 2 years after symptom onset1, 2. Historically, open heart surgery was the only treatment for severe AS. However, advanced age was a dominant argument to defer surgery. Transcatheter aortic valve implantation (TAVI) was contrived as a less invasive alternative to surgery and to fulfill this unmet clinical need. After the first-in-human procedure in 2002, TAVI matured into a guideline recommended treatment of symptomatic severe AS in elderly patients across the entire risk spectrum3-7. Peri-procedural embolization Operator experience, improved planning and implantation strategies and multiple device iterations including smaller profile, repositioning ability and outer sealing fabric converted TAVI into a reproducible and relatively safe procedure8. However, the “Big Five” of complications in the modern TAVI era remain 1) access site complications and bleedings, 2) paravalvular leakage (PVL), 3) acute kidney injury (AKI), 4) conduction disturbances including the need for permanent pacemaker implantation (PPI) and 5) stroke9. Up to 5% of patients suffer a neurological event after TAVI, mainly within the first 48 hours8, 10, 11. This finding suggests a direct causative role with the transcatheter valve implantation itself. Transcranial Doppler and brain Magnetic Resonance Imaging (MRI) studies revealed debris embolization towards the brain and new brain lesions after TAVI in the vast majority of patients12-15. Most of these embolizations remain clinically silent at first sight but may be linked to neurocognitive decline and frank dementia16. Embolic protection devices (EPD) have been developed to deflect or capture embolized debris on its way to the brain and may possibly reduce brain lesions and neurological events including stroke and neurocognitive decline. Part I of this thesis adds perspective to the etiopathology of TAVI related stroke and the mechanism of action of the current spectrum of cerebral embolic protection devices. We also present insights into the microscopic analysis of debris that was captured with filters during TAVI procedures. Vascular access and complications 1 TAVI typically requires large bore femoral artery access. By default, larger arteriotomies are at higher risk for access site complications and bleedings. A completely percutaneous approach relies on vascular access closure devices (VCD) to manage the arteriotomy and provide patent hemostasis. TAVI in low to intermediate risk patients is associated with a major vascular complication rate ranging between 2 and 8%4, 11. The conventional closure technique is based on sutures and most access site complications after TAVI procedures are related to closure device failure17. A collagen plug based closure device was introduced as an alternative to sutures. Part II of this thesis addresses vascular complications and provides information on clinical outcomes with collagen plug-based VCD. TAVI-related conduction disturbances Acquired conduction disturbances after TAVI are frequent and may lead to heart failure (re-) admissions and impaired long-term prognosis18-22. The atrioventricular bundle pierces the membranous septum between the right and non-coronary cusp of the aortic valve and surfaces along the left ventricular outflow tract (LVOT), which makes it vulnerable to contact pressure by the implanted transcatheter heart valve (THV) during TAVI23, 24. New left bundle branch block (LBBB) and third-degree atrioventricular block (AV3B) requiring PPI occur in up to a third and quarter of patients, respectively18-22. These conduction disturbances may be transient or remain permanent which is clinically relevant in view of in-hospital stay and overall healthcare costs. Unfortunately, there are no uniform definitions to describe conduction dynamics post-TAVI. Inconsistent reporting makes the interpretation of the literature on this topic challenging. Part III of this thesis will elaborate on what is currently known about the incidence of newly acquired conduction disturbances after TAVI and studies specific features on the baseline and postprocedural electrocardiogram (ECG) to predict conduction dynamics. These insights may help determine the need and timing of PPI and adjust hospital discharge policies.

title: Diastolic Dysfunction in Congenital Heart Disease: A Pressure-Volume Loop Analysis of Borderline Left Heart
authors: Nikhil M. Thatte; Martin Liberman; Peter E. Hammer; Ryan M. Callahan; Jesse J. Esch; Michael Farias; Gerald Ross Marx; Rebecca Sussanne Beroukhim; Eric N. Feins; Sitaram M. Emani; Sunil J. Ghelani
abstract: Abstract Background Diastolic dysfunction is a major driver of morbidity in congenital heart disease (CHD), but its mechanisms are poorly understood. It remains unknown whether left ventricular (LV) diastolic dysfunction in borderline left heart patients is caused by a defect in active relaxation or in passive compliance. Objectives We sought to apply gold-standard pressure-volume (PV) loop analysis to define the primary mechanism of diastolic dysfunction in patients with borderline LV (bLV). Methods We analyzed invasive PV loop data from pediatric patients with bLV (n =13) and a comparison group of patients with congenitally corrected transposition of the great arteries (ccTGA, presumed no diastolic dysfunction; n=14). PV loops were generated during transient preload reduction and augmentation. Active relaxation was assessed by the isovolumic relaxation time-constant (τ) and maximal rate of pressure decline (dP/dt min ) indexed to peak-systolic pressure (PSP). Passive compliance was quantified by the chamber stiffness constant (β), derived from the multi-beat end-diastolic PV relationship (EDPVR). To account for size differences, β was (1) calculated using indexed ventricular volumes (iβ), and (2) converted to a dimensionless stiffness constant (β W ) by multiplying β by ventricular wall volume. Results Active relaxation measures were similar between groups, indicating normal lusitropy in bLV (τ bLV: 28 [23.5-29.5] vs ccTGA: 24 [21-28] msec, p=0.10; dP/dt min /PSP bLV: -10.6 [-11.0, -9.4] vs. ccTGA: -9.9 [-10.5, -8.7] s -1 , p=0.17). In contrast, patients with bLV had markedly abnormal passive compliance. The EDPVR was shifted sharply upward and to the left, and the stiffness constants were significantly higher in the bLV group (iβ bLV: 0.10 [0.04-0.35] vs. ccTGA: 0.03 [0.02-0.04] m 2 /mL, p=0.003); β W bLV: 4.08 [1.60-7.52] vs. ccTGA: 1.21 [0.95-1.77], p=0.002). Conclusions The primary mechanism of diastolic dysfunction in bLV is impaired passive ventricular compliance, and not impaired active relaxation. These findings suggest a limited role for lusitropic medications and therapeutic strategies that focus on mitigating ventricular stiffness (such as surgical endocardial fibroelastosis resection) may be more valuable. Condensed abstract Pressure-volume loop analysis with preload alteration in pediatric congenital heart disease shows that in borderline left heart patients left ventricular diastolic dysfunction is caused by impaired passive compliance, with preserved active relaxation. This mechanistic insight suggests that interventions targeting ventricular stiffness such as surgical endocardial fibroelastosis resection may be more beneficial than the use of lusitropic medications to improve outcomes.

title: Technical development and implementation of 3D‐QALAS on a 1.5T MR‐Linac for the brain: A prospective R‐IDEAL stage 0/1 technology development report
authors: Lucas B. McCullum; Ashley Harrington; Natalie A. West; Grace Nehring; Clifton D. Fuller; Ergys Subashi; Brian A. Taylor; Ken‐Pin Hwang; Clifton David Fuller
journal: Journal of Applied Clinical Medical Physics
abstract: BACKGROUND: Quantitative relaxometry of the brain on the integrated MRI / linear accelerator (MR-Linac) at high isotropic reconstructed resolution is currently limited due to prohibitively long scan times and limited field-of-views. PURPOSE: The purpose of this study was to assess the technical feasibility of the 3D-QALAS technique on the 1.5T MR-Linac which can acquire whole-brain 1 mm isotropic quantitative T1, T2, and PD maps along with multiple synthetic images in a 7-minute acquisition time. METHODS: A 1 mm isotropic 3D-QALAS acquisition was scanned in both phantoms and five healthy volunteers on the 1.5T Elekta Unity MR-Linac device with scan times around seven minutes. A test-retest protocol across five independent sessions for the phantom was conducted. The Lin's Concordance Correlation Coefficient (LCCC), repeatability, and reproducibility between measured and reference quantitative T1, T2, and PD values were determined in the phantom. Distortion was also studied. Vendor-provided reconstruction through SyMRI was performed to extract synthetic images and brain volume metric assessments in the healthy volunteers. RESULTS: The slope and LCCC between the measured and phantom reference values was 1.02 (1.00), 1.09 (0.90), and 0.99 (1.00) for T1, T2, and PD, respectively. Median distortion across the phantom remained below 2 mm. The repeatability and reproducibility coefficient-of-variation (CoV) was under 8% for all measured values. The measured brain volumes in the healthy volunteer was within expected age-adjusted reference values. CONCLUSIONS: The technical feasibility of using 3D-QALAS on the integrated 1.5T MR-Linac was confirmed. Applying this technique to the adaptive radiation therapy workflow of the brain will provide new opportunities to integrate quantitative imaging relaxometry biomarkers at 1 mm isotropic reconstructed resolution.

title: T-Cell–Derived IFNγ Instructs ECM Crosslinking by Cardiac Fibroblasts Through LOXL3 in Experimental Cardiometabolic HFpEF
authors: Ramona Emig; Zachary L. Robbe; Celina Kley; Sasha A. Smolgovsky; Abraham L. Bayer; Joshua G. Travers; Robert M. Blanton; Timothy A. McKinsey; Lauren Deems Black; Pilar Alcaide
abstract: Abstract Background Heart failure with preserved ejection fraction (HFpEF) is a major clinical challenge characterized by diastolic dysfunction. Left ventricular stiffening and inflammation are hallmarks of HFpEF, yet the contribution of extracellular matrix (ECM) stiffness and the immune–stromal mechanisms driving ECM stiffening in cardiometabolic HFpEF remain poorly understood. Methods We used the murine “2-hit model” of cardiometabolic HFpEF, in which the combination of high fat diet and hypertension induced by L-NAME causes diastolic dysfunction. We evaluated diastolic function by echocardiography and ECM mechanics by uniaxial tensile testing of decellularized cardiac tissue. Functional in vivo studies included genetic depletion of T cells, interferon-γ (IFNγ) knockout mice, and pharmacological lysyl oxidase inhibition. We combined co-cultures of CD4 + T cells and cardiac fibroblasts (CFB) with mechanical testing of cardiac ECM and molecular biology to elucidate cellular and molecular mechanisms. Results Left ventricular ECM stiffness strongly correlated with impaired diastolic function in experimental cardiometabolic HFpEF. Cardiac CD4⁺ T cell infiltration was required for ECM stiffening and upregulation of lysyl oxidase enzymes in CFB. CD4 + T cell-derived IFNγ was both necessary and sufficient to induce LOXL3 in CFB, which increased ECM stiffness in vitro . Mechanistically, IFNγ signaling activated hypoxia-inducible factor-1α (HIF1α) in CFB, driving LOXL3 expression and subsequent collagen crosslinking. Genetic or pharmacologic disruption of this IFNγ–HIF1α–LOXL3 axis in vivo attenuated adverse ECM remodeling and improved diastolic function. Conclusions CD4⁺ T cells promote pathological ECM stiffening in cardiometabolic HFpEF through IFNγ-mediated, LOXL3-dependent ECM crosslinking by CFB. Targeting this immune–stromal pathway may offer a novel therapeutic strategy for HFpEF.

title: Клинико-экономический анализ транскатетерной имплантации в сравнении с хирургической заменой аортального клапана у пациентов низкого риска в Российской Федерации
authors: Огнерубов Дмитрий Викторович; Мершин Кирилл Вячеславович; Курбанов Гамид Магомедсаламович; Берсенева Евгения Александровна; Меркулов Евгений Владимирович
abstract: Проведен клинико-экономический анализ транскатетерной имплантации аортального клапана (ТИАК) в сравнении с хирургической заменой аортального клапана (ХЗАК) у пациентов с тяжелым аортальным стенозом низкого хирургического риска в условиях системы здравоохранения Российской Федерации. Проведено ретроспективное клинико-экономическое моделирование с 5-летним горизонтом. Данные для группы ХЗАК (n = 208) были получены ретроспективно из базы данных одного кардиохирургического центра (ФГБУ “Национальный медицинский исследовательский центр кардиологии им. акад. Е.И. Чазова” Минздрава России, 2019–2024 годы). В связи с отсутствием репрезентативных локальных данных по ТИАК у пациентов низкого риска клинические исходы (летальность, инсульт, повторная госпитализация) для группы ТИАК (n = 496) были взяты из 5-летних результатов исследования PARTNER 3. Экономическая оценка, включавшая анализ коэффициентов “затраты/эффективность” и “затраты/полезность”, проводилась с использованием российских тарифов и дисконтированием затрат (5%). Пятилетняя дисконтированная стоимость ХЗАК составила 1 051 088 руб., ТИАК – 2 149 365 руб. Локальная когорта ХЗАК продемонстрировала лучшие 5-летние клинические исходы по сравнению с данными ТИАК из PARTNER 3, включая более низкую летальность (5,8 против 10,0%), частоту инсультов (1,92 против 5,8%; p = 0,015) и больших кровотечений (2,9 против 10,2%; p = 0,0003). Группа ХЗАК также набрала больше лет жизни с поправкой на качество (quality-adjusted life year, QALY) за 5-летний период (4,14 против 3,88 года). Инкрементный показатель “затраты/полезность” был отрицательным (–4 224 142 руб./QALY), что характеризует ТИАК как доминируемую технологию (более дорогую и менее эффективную). В рамках данной 5-летней модели, основанной на локальных данных ХЗАК и тарифах РФ, ХЗАК является экономически доминирующей стратегией лечения пациентов низкого хирургического риска по сравнению с ТИАК.

title: Afterload-Adjusted Strain Refines Risk Stratification in Aortic Stenosis With Varying Degrees of Aortic Regurgitation
authors: Jonghee Sun; Jiesuck Park; Hyoung-Won Cho; Minjung Bak; Hong‐Mi Choi; In‐Chang Hwang; Yeonyee Elizabeth Yoon; Goo‐Yeong Cho

title: Association of haematologic parameters with persistent rheumatic heart disease stage in children: a pilot study
authors: G.N. Kalay; Sevim Aslı Ehlil; Ali Karakaş; Samed Cihad Celik; Nergis Akay; Büşra Albayrak; Hazal Cansu Çulpan; İlker Kemal Yücel; Özgür Kasapçopur; Reyhan Dedeoğlu
abstract: Abstract Purpose: Rheumatic heart disease remains a major cause of cardiovascular morbidity in children. Although echocardiography is central to diagnosis and staging, it does not directly reflect inflammatory processes that may contribute to ongoing valvular damage. This study aimed to evaluate the association between baseline haematologic parameters and persistent rheumatic heart disease stage in children with prior acute rheumatic fever. Methods: In this single-centre retrospective pilot study, 45 children with persistent rheumatic heart disease were classified as Stage A ( n = 23), Stage B ( n = 14), or Stage C ( n = 8) according to the 2023 World Heart Federation echocardiographic staging framework. Baseline laboratory values obtained during acute presentation were analysed. Clinical and laboratory variables were compared across stages using non-parametric tests. Binary logistic regression identified factors associated with advanced disease (Stage B–C vs Stage A). Results: Markers reflecting acute inflammatory activity, including leukocyte counts and derived indices, did not differ significantly among stages. In contrast, red cell distribution width, mean platelet volume, and platelet distribution width differed significantly. In multivariable analysis, red cell distribution width, and mean platelet volume were independently associated with advanced persistent rheumatic heart disease stage, with higher values linked to increased odds of Stage B–C disease. Conclusion: Red cell distribution width and mean platelet volume were associated with advanced stages of persistent paediatric rheumatic heart disease. These widely available haematologic markers may complement echocardiographic assessment. Larger prospective studies are needed to define their clinical utility. Trial registration: Not applicable (retrospective study).

title: Integrative multi-omics and machine learning identify mechanical stimulus-related genes and immune microenvironment remodeling in heart failure
authors: Cheng Zhang; Linna Zhao; Jiahuan Sun; Xiaodan Wang; Chuang Zhang; Aiying Li
abstract: Background Heart failure (HF) is a leading cause of global morbidity and mortality, driven by complex pathophysiological processes including abnormal mechanical stress and immune microenvironment remodeling. Although mechanical stimulus is known to trigger maladaptive cardiac remodeling, the systematic role of mechanical stimulus-related genes (MSRGs) in HF diagnosis and immune modulation remains poorly defined. This study aims to identify MSRG-based diagnostic biomarkers, characterize molecular subtypes, and explore their cellular localization and immune microenvironment interactions in HF. Methods Bulk transcriptomic data and MSigDB-curated MSRGs were analyzed. Differential expression screening identified MSRGs altered between HF and healthy specimens. Three algorithms—Random Forest, LASSO, and SVM-RFE—were jointly applied to select diagnostic biomarkers and build a nomogram. Consensus clustering defined MSRG-based subtypes, with immune profiles compared across groups. Single-cell sequencing localized key biomarkers in cardiac tissues. A transverse aortic constriction (TAC)-induced rat HF model served for in vivo validation via RT-qPCR, Western blotting, and immunohistochemistry. Results A total of 53 MSRG-related DEGs were identified, from which 11 core diagnostic biomarkers were selected. The nomogram model showed high predictive performance. Consensus clustering revealed two distinct HF subtypes: Cluster A exhibited enhanced metabolic and homeostatic pathways, while Cluster B showed pronounced extracellular matrix remodeling and fibrotic features, with differential immune infiltration. Single-cell analysis demonstrated CASP1 enrichment in macrophages/monocytes and PTN/MDK enrichment in fibroblasts. In vivo validation confirmed significant upregulation of PTN, MDK, and CASP1 at both mRNA and protein levels in TAC hearts, alongside elevated pro-inflammatory cytokines (IL-6, IL-1β) and fibrotic markers, linking mechanical stimulus-related genes to local inflammation and adverse remodeling. Conclusion MSRGs serve as robust diagnostic biomarkers for HF and enable the identification of two molecular subtypes with distinct immune microenvironment and biological pathway profiles. The CASP1-MDK-PTN axis emerges as a potential pathogenic cascade connecting mechanical stress to inflammatory and fibrotic remodeling. These findings provide a framework for early molecular subtyping, improved risk stratification, and targeted immunomodulatory therapy in HF.

title: Distinct Biomarker Signatures of CMR-Defined Myocardial Remodeling in Moderate Aortic Stenosis
authors: Jan M. Wrobel; Jan Paul Janßen; Alina Beckmann; Jasmin Shamekhi; Mohammed Bahaaeldin; Julian Alexander Luetkens; Ibrahim Hawwari; Stephan Nienaber; Bernardo Franklin; Malte Kelm; Georg Nickenig; David C. Maintz; Stephan Ernst Baldus; Tobias Zeus; Lenhard Pennig; Victor Mauri
abstract: Background: Moderate aortic stenosis (AS) is associated with adverse outcomes, yet the myocardial response to pressure overload varies substantially between patients and is incompletely reflected by valve hemodynamics. We aimed to determine whether circulating biomarkers of myocardial stress, injury, and fibrosis associate with cardiac magnetic resonance (CMR)-defined myocardial remodeling in moderate AS. Methods: Eighty-nine patients with moderate AS prospectively underwent CMR (cine imaging, T1 mapping, extracellular volume fraction [ECV], late gadolinium enhancement [LGE]) with concurrent measurement of NT-proBNP, high-sensitivity troponin T, sST2, TIMP-1, and Galectin-3. Biomarker associations with the phenotype-defining CMR parameters were tested with adjustment for age, sex, and renal function and correction for multiple testing, and patients were additionally classified into 4 hierarchical remodeling phenotypes. Results: Six of 20 biomarker-CMR associations remained significant after correction for multiple testing. NT-proBNP tracked LV mass index (beta=0.50), ECV (beta=0.35), and LGE burden (beta=0.43, all q<0.05). TIMP-1 and Galectin-3 were selectively associated with native T1 (both beta=0.35, q=0.012), and sST2 was inversely associated with LV mass index (beta=-0.27, q=0.046). TIMP-1 (adjusted OR 2.18 per SD, 95% CI 1.37-3.48, q=0.005) and NT-proBNP (OR 2.10, 1.19-3.69, q=0.026) increased with higher hierarchical remodeling phenotype. No biomarker was associated with echocardiographic mean gradient, peak velocity, or indexed valve area after correction. Conclusions: Circulating biomarkers showed distinct associations with CMR measures of myocardial remodeling in moderate AS. Matrix-related biomarkers were associated with native T1, whereas NT-proBNP was associated across several remodeling domains. These signals were not measurably related to valve hemodynamics.

title: Diffuse coronary vasospasm causing refractory ventricular fibrillation after minimally invasive mitral valve replacement in a patient with anomalous right coronary artery: a case report
authors: Jie Wu; Tu'erhong Fei'erdun; 路万里
abstract: Malignant arrhythmias and circulatory failure after heart valve surgery are most commonly associated with inadequate myocardial protection, electrolyte disturbances, and prosthetic valve dysfunction. In contrast, isolated diffuse coronary vasospasm is a rare peri-operative complication with substantial risk of life-threatening cardiogenic shock and high early mortality when unrecognized. Anomalous origin of the right coronary artery (RCA) arising from the left coronary sinus represents a rare congenital coronary anatomical variant, which may confer increased susceptibility to peri-operative vasospasm under surgical physiological stress. Furthermore, this abnormal ostial location frequently results in technical difficulty for selective guide-catheter engagement during emergency coronary angiography, limiting local intracoronary vasodilator delivery and rendering pharmacologic management particularly challenging in acute postoperative scenarios. Herein, we report a case of diffuse coronary vasospasm following rheumatic valve surgery in a patient with an anomalous right coronary artery originating from the left coronary sinus, and summarize our diagnostic and therapeutic experience to provide a reference for similar clinical scenarios. A 58-year-old man with a 10-year history of rheumatic heart disease and hypertension was admitted with cough, sputum production, palpitations, and orthopnea. The preoperative diagnoses included rheumatic mitral stenosis, persistent atrial fibrillation, left atrial thrombus, tricuspid regurgitation, and an anomalous RCA arising from the left coronary sinus without significant stenosis. The patient underwent minimally invasive mitral valve replacement along with concomitant procedures. After aortic declamping, he developed ventricular arrhythmias, global myocardial hypokinesia, and failed to wean from cardiopulmonary bypass, requiring venoarterial extracorporeal membrane oxygenation (VA-ECMO) support. In the intensive care unit (ICU), recurrent ventricular arrhythmias accompanied by ST-segment elevation were observed. Emergency coronary angiography demonstrated diffuse coronary vasospasm. The spasm in the left coronary system resolved after administration of vasodilators, whereas the anomalous RCA showed a poor response to intracoronary drug therapy. Emergency coronary artery bypass grafting was subsequently performed. The patient recovered uneventfully and was discharged with normal cardiac function. Diffuse coronary vasospasm represents a rare but life-threatening complication following cardiac valve surgery and may lead to refractory circulatory collapse. When this complication occurs in patients with congenital anomalous coronary anatomy, pharmacological therapy is prone to failure due to challenges in targeted intracoronary drug delivery. Timely surgical revascularization should therefore be considered early and may prove life-saving for these high-risk individuals.

title: Ultra-high-resolution Photon-Counting CT for Leaflet-Specific Evaluation of Fibrosis and Calcification in Aortic Stenosis
authors: Mohammed Bahaaeldin; Jasmin Shamekhi; Bernardo S. Franklin; Sebastian Nowak; Alexander M.C. Bohner; Dmitrij Kravchenko; Jan M. Wrobel; Raphael Phinicarides; Lenhard Pennig; Jan Paul Janßen; Carsten Gietzen; Sebastian Zimmer; Stephan Ernst Baldus; Malte Kelm; Georg Nickenig; Tobias Zeus; Victor Mauri; Julian Alexander Luetkens
abstract: Objectives: Ultra-high-resolution photon-counting detector (PCD)-CT may enable leaflet-specific analysis of aortic valve fibrosis and calcification, providing insights into early aortic stenosis (AS) disease progression. This study aimed to investigate how PCD-CT leaflet-specific calcific and fibrotic volumes influence cardiovascular magnetic resonance (CMR) leaflet mobility. Materials and methods: Participants with moderate aortic AS prospectively underwent both PCD-CT (n=80) and CMR (n=58). Using PCD-CT, calcific and fibrotic volumes were segmented for right (RCC), left (LCC), and non-coronary cusps (NCC) and indexed to the aortic annulus area (ICV and IFV). CMR-derived leaflet mobility index (LMI) was assessed. Two raters compared image quality using a Likert scale (1=poor to 5=excellent) and distinguishability of individual leaflets in PCD-CT with EID-CT (n=82). Results: PCD-CT analysis showed that calcification was higher in males (e.g., ICVRCC: 15+/-16 vs. 4+/-7 uL/cm^2; p<0.001), while fibrosis was higher in females (e.g., IFVLCC: 47+/-18 vs. 34+/-15 uL/cm^2; p=0.004) across all leaflets. Fibrocalcific ratio was higher in LCC (53+/-276) compared to RCC (19+/-48; p<0.001) and NCC (13.5+/-34; p<0.001). LMI of RCC was higher in females compared to men (0.66+/-0.21 vs. 0.38+/-0.33; p=0.008). LMILCC and LMINCC showed no sex differences. LMIRCC negatively correlated with ICVRCC (ρ=-0.64 [-0.77, -0.46]; p<0.001) and LMINCC with ICVNCC (ρ=-0.69 [-0.80, -0.53]; p<0.001), whereas LMILCC negatively correlated with IFVLCC (ρ=-0.35 [-0.56, -0.10]; p=0.007), particularly in females (ρ=-0.70 [-0.89, -0.31]; p=0.003). PCD-CT yielded higher image quality (5 [IQR 4-5] vs. 3 [3-4]; p<0.001) and leaflet distinguishability (79/80 [99%] vs. 42/82 [51%]; p<0.001) than EID-CT. Conclusions: Ultra-high-resolution PCD-CT allows for leaflet-specific quantification of indexed fibrotic and calcific volume. These volumes demonstrate sex- and leaflet-specific differences that may distinctly contribute to AS pathophysiology.

title: Long-term clinical and echocardiographic outcomes after mitral valve surgery for severe mitral annular calcification
authors: Yoganiranjana Dharuman; Egan Leonidovich Kalmykov; Mirko Doss
abstract: Objective To assess the long-term clinical and echocardiographic outcomes of mitral valve surgery with annular decalcification and pericardial patch reconstruction in patients with severe mitral annular calcification (MAC). Patients and methods Between 2012 and 2022, 112 consecutive high-risk patients (67 women, 45 men; mean age 66.5 ± 13.6 years) underwent surgery for severe MAC with mitral stenosis and/or regurgitation. Mitral valve repair was performed in 55 patients (49%) and replacement in 57 (51%). Concomitant procedures were performed in 65 patients (58%). Mean follow-up was 97 ± 48 months. Results Early mortality was 6.3% ( n = 7) and late mortality was 23.2% ( n = 26). Survival was 89.3%, 77.2%, and 64.1% at 60, 96, and 144 months, respectively. Freedom from reoperation was 98.3% at 60 months and 93.3% at 96 months. At follow-up, no surviving patient had more than grade III mitral regurgitation. Grade III regurgitation was present in 3 patients (4%), while no patient had grade IV regurgitation. Left atrial diameter, left ventricular end-diastolic diameter, and mean transvalvular gradient were significantly lower than before surgery. Conclusion In this high-risk cohort, annular decalcification and pericardial patch reconstruction provided durable valve function and acceptable long-term survival in patients who survived the perioperative period. Perioperative mortality, however, remained substantial.

title: Outcomes of transcatheter aortic valve implantation using evolut self-expanding valves at Cardiovascular Center – E Hospital
authors: Thao Nguyen Phan; The Huy Nguyen; Hai Son Dam; Đức Ngọc Lý
journal: Tạp chí Phẫu thuật và Tim mạch và Lồng ngực Việt Nam
abstract: Objectives: To evaluate the procedural outcomes, safety, and clinical efficacy of Transcatheter Aortic Valve Implantation (TAVI) using the Evolut self-expanding valve system in patients with severe aortic stenosis at E Hospital. Methods: A descriptive, longitudinal study was conducted on 21 patients undergoing TAVI from December 2019 to December 2025. Results: The mean age was 72.2 ± 8.3 years; males accounted for 52.4%. Complex characteristics included bicuspid aortic valves (33.3%), degenerated bioprosthetic valves (Valve-in-Valve) (19.0%), and concomitant coronary artery disease requiring Chimney stenting (23.8%). The mean EuroSCORE II was 5.2 ± 1.8%, and the STS Score was 4.1 ± 1.5%. Regarding hemodynamics, the effective orifice area (EOA) increased from 0.65 ± 0.15 cm² to 1.85 ± 0.45 cm²; the mean pressure gradient decreased from 55 ± 12 mmHg to 8.5 ± 3.2 mmHg. The procedural volume increased over time, peaking with 9 cases in 2025. In-hospital mortality was 9.5% (2 cases); both occurred in the early phase (2020 and 2023) associated with highly complex anatomy. Moderate paravalvular leak was observed in 1 case (4.8%), and there were no cases of conduction disorders requiring a permanent pacemaker (0%). No major complications were recorded in the 2024–2025 period. At the 6-month follow-up, left ventricular ejection fraction (EF) improved from 57.38 ± 12.1% to 60.15 ± 9.8%. Conclusion: TAVI using Evolut self-expanding valves is a feasible and effective procedure at E Hospital. Despite initial challenges related to the learning curve, the current protocol has been standardized with high safety outcomes. The role of the Heart Team in patient selection and thorough anatomical assessment is the key factor in improving treatment outcomes.

title: Ultra-high-pitch photon-counting computed tomography (PCCT) versus ultra-high-pitch dual-source computed tomography (DSCT) for coronary artery disease evaluation in transcatheter aortic valve implantation (TAVI) patients
authors: Ines Mecking; Marc von der Stück; Eric Corban; Michael Frick; Jörg W. Schröder; Roman Iwa; Christiane Katharina Kuhl; Timm Dirrichs
abstract: Rationale and objectives To compare radiation dose and image quality of coronary artery reconstructions obtained from non–coronary-dedicated transcatheter aortic valve implantation (TAVI) planning CT scans using ultra-high-pitch photon-counting CT (PCCT) and ultra-high-pitch energy-integrating detector dual-source CT (EID-DSCT; hereafter referred to as DSCT), including assessment of the feasibility of coronary artery evaluation according to the Coronary Artery Disease Reporting and Data System (CAD-RADS). Materials and methods Retrospective study on consecutive patients with aortic valve stenosis (AS) undergoing contrast-enhanced TAVI planning CT, either PCCT or DSCT between August 2021 and June 2023. CT dose index (CTDI) and dose length product (DLP) were used to calculate the effective radiation dose (eRD). Signal-to-noise ratio (SNR) and contrast-to-noise ratio (CNR) were calculated using standardized region-of-interest (ROI) analysis. Coronary arteries were evaluated by three independent radiologists using 5-point Likert scales followed by a classification according to the CAD-RADS system. Results 187 patients (83 female, median age 82, IQR: 76–84) underwent 190 CT-examinations, 103 PCCT (54.2%) and 87 (45.8%) DSCT. Three patients underwent both PCCT and DSCT for clinical reasons. Mean CTDI and DLP were significantly lower in PCCT compared to DSCT (21.9 vs. 52.8 and 607.9 vs. 906.8, respectively; both p < 0.001), with a correspondingly lower mean effective radiation dose (eRD) in PCCT compared to DSCT (10.3 ± 5.4 mSv vs. 15.4 ± 5.6 mSv, p < 0.001). While both SNR and CNR were lower in PCCT than in DSCT (SNR: 35.28 ± 11.63 in PCCT vs. 45.6 ± 16.3 in DSCT, p < 0.001; CNR: 49.25 ± 13.31 in PCCT vs. 57.42 v ± 22.55 in DSCT, p = 0.004), PCCT outperformed DSCT in every one of the eleven visual image categories. Overall image quality was rated as good or excellent in 71.8% (74/103) of PCCT vs. 19.5% (17/87) of DSCT scans. Coronary reconstructions were rated as good or excellent in 72.8% (75/103) of PCCT vs. 20.7% of DSCT datasets. CAD-RADS [1–5] rating was possible in 68.9% (71/103) of PCCT vs. 39.1% (34/87) of DSCT datasets. Conclusion Photon-counting computed tomography (PCCT) allows for significantly improved assessability of the coronary arteries in TAVI planning CT compared with dual-source CT (DSCT), while achieving a substantially lower radiation dose.

title: From TAVR to SAVR
authors: Karen Hovsepyan; Amy Hutchinson; Michael Finamore; Lucas Henn
journal: Translation The University of Toledo Journal of Medical Sciences
abstract: Background:Transcatheter aortic valve replacement (TAVR) is an established minimally invasive therapy for severe aortic stenosis, with a steadily declining incidence of procedural complications. Nevertheless, emergent conversion to surgical aortic valve replacement (SAVR), although rare, remains associated with substantial morbidity and mortality. Case Summary:A 71-year-old male with severe aortic stenosis and multiple comorbidities underwent elective transfemoral TAVR using a 26-mm SAPIEN 3 Ultra Resilia valve. Initial post-deployment imaging demonstrated satisfactory valve position and hemodynamic performance. On postoperative day 0, the patient developed severe hypertension followed by embolization of the bioprosthetic valve into the left ventricular outflow tract (LVOT), resulting in obstruction and interference with the mitral valve apparatus. Given the risk of hemodynamic collapse, the patient was taken emergently for explant of the TAVR . Intraoperative findings revealed a migrated and rotated transcatheter valve causing partial LVOT obstruction and laceration of the ventricular side of the anterior mitral valve leaflet. The valve was successfully explanted, and surgical aortic valve replacement was performed. The postoperative course was complicated by transient acute kidney injury, which resolved prior to discharge on postoperative day 9. Conclusion:This case illustrates a rare but life-threatening complication of TAVR requiring emergent surgical intervention and highlights the importance of vigilant monitoring, strict hemodynamic control, and immediate surgical readiness.

title: From Reduced Order Models to ATLAS: A Real‐Time Platform for Hemodynamics
authors: Zahra Mirzaiyan; Davide Oberto; Pierfrancesco Siena; Gianluigi Rozza
abstract: ABSTRACT Cardiovascular diseases represent one of the leading causes of death worldwide, leading to the development of advanced research in numerical analysis to create decision‐support tools for the clinical community. The main objective is to develop advanced numerical frameworks for accurate diagnosis and personalized treatment planning. While high‐fidelity computational fluid dynamics (CFD) simulations provide detailed hemodynamic insights, their high computational cost, due to the large number of degrees of freedom and complex morphologies involved, limits their use in real‐time clinical routine. Reduced order models (ROMs) have emerged as a powerful framework to overcome these limitations by providing accurate approximations at a significantly reduced computational cost. In this paper, we provide a high‐level overview of the main ROM methodological categories, including linear and nonlinear approaches, and refer to relevant literature for more comprehensive treatments. Despite their potential, the technical complexity and specialized expertise required to implement these methods often hinder their direct application in clinical settings. To overcome these limitations, we introduce ATLAS, a cloud‐native open‐access platform designed to bridge the gap between complex numerical modeling and clinical practice through an intuitive web interface. The potential of the platform is demonstrated through a case study on the left atrial appendage (LAA), focusing on blood stasis as a key indicator of stroke risk. Finally, we discuss the role of ROMs as a key enabling technology for the development of cardiovascular digital twins, highlighting the potential for bidirectional communication between physical patients and their virtual counterparts.

title: Study protocol for a prospective multicenter longitudinal cohort study on progression of moderate aortic valve stenosis, the MODAS Study
authors: Raphael Phinicarides; Kathrin Klein; Christian Jung; Bernardo S. Franklin; Ibrahim Hawwari; Victor Mauri; Jan M. Wrobel; Stephan E. Baldus; Julian A. Luetkens; Jasmin Shamekhi; Georg Nickenig; Verena Veulemans; Malte Kelm; Tobias Zeus
abstract: Background: Calcific aortic stenosis (AS) is one of the most common and prognostically relevant valvular heart diseases, with a growing global burden driven by population ageing. Prediction of disease progression from moderate to severe AS, which would be instrumental for earlier diagnosis and treatment, remains challenging. At the same time, moderate AS is increasingly recognized as a heterogeneous condition associated with clinically relevant risk, particularly in patients with cardiac damage, heart failure, or rapid disease progression. Conventional echocardiographic parameters incompletely capture the biological heterogeneity underlying AS progression. The MODAS study was established to investigate biomarkers and mechanisms of AS progression and outcome using longitudinal multimodal phenotyping. Methods: The MODAS Study is a prospective, multicenter, longitudinal observational cohort study enrolling adults with moderate calcific tricuspid AS at three tertiary heart valve centers in Germany. Participants undergo standardized baseline assessment including clinical phenotyping, laboratory testing, electrocardiography, transthoracic echocardiography, cardiac computed tomography and cardiac magnetic resonance imaging. Biospecimens are collected for biomarker, immunologic, proteomic, and genetic analyses, including genome-wide association studies and assessment of clonal haematopoiesis. Participants are followed annually for up to 5 years with repeat clinical assessment, laboratory testing, and echocardiography. The primary endpoint is time to progression to severe AS according to 2025 ESC/EACTS guideline criteria or aortic valve replacement for severe AS, adjudicated by the local multidisciplinary Heart Team. Secondary endpoints include all-cause mortality and additional clinical outcome trajectories. Multimodal data integration will be used to develop and validate prediction models for disease progression and outcome. Discussion: The MODAS Study will provide a harmonized, deeply phenotyped longitudinal dataset to improve risk stratification in moderate AS and to identify imaging, inflammatory, and genetic markers associated with rapid progression and adverse outcomes. The study is designed to support future personalized surveillance strategies, improved selection for earlier intervention, and mechanistic understanding of calcific AS progression. Trial registration: ClinicalTrials.gov NCT05851209 . Registered on 9 May 2023.
